memos.headline: S08 and S02 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S04 and S07 Show Structural Weakness
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market today. S08 is sitting at its 52-week high with RSI 71.6 and +19.8% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks — this is the strongest momentum name in the universe, though the extended RSI means I'd want to buy pullbacks toward the 50-day mean (~302) rather than chase here. S02 is nearly as compelling: +23.1% over 12 weeks, only -1.3% from its high, RSI a comfortable 57.9, and +17.6% relative strength over 12 weeks — trend is firmly intact and I'd stay long above ~400. On the weak side, S04 is -27.3% from its 52-week high and trading 10.4% below its 200-day mean, a textbook downtrend with only a tepid bounce (RSI 51.9); I'd avoid until it reclaims the 200-day. S07 dropped 7.6% this week alone, RSI is 40.1, and it's -17.3% from highs despite a strong 26-week return — this looks like a momentum reversal in progress, and the 5.12% ATR makes it treacherous; I'd need a close back above the 50-day (~928) to reconsider.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 Margin Collapse Is a Red Flag
memos.body: I am most convicted on the top end and bottom end of this universe. S10 posted 85.2% YoY revenue growth to $81.6B with a 71.5% net margin and only $8.5B of total debt—this is the cleanest earnings profile I see, though the pace of growth invites mean-reversion risk. S05 delivered $62.6B of net income on $109.9B of revenue (56.9% margin) with net income up 81.2% YoY and minimal leverage at $14.8B of debt, making it the second-best quality name. On the other side, S09's net income fell 45.8% YoY to $4.2B on essentially flat revenue (+2.4%), compressing the net margin to just 4.9%—I need to see margin stabilization before getting constructive. S02 is similarly sluggish at +2.0% revenue growth and a thin 5.6% margin with $77.9B of debt, offering no earnings catalyst. S04 and S03 sit in a solid middle tier with double-digit revenue growth and healthy margins, though S03's $122.6B debt load warrants monitoring.

views.note: 85% YoY revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, and only $8.5B debt represent the strongest earnings power in the universe; a margin decline below 50% would change my view.
56.9% net margin with 81.2% YoY net income growth and minimal $14.8B debt make this a durable high-quality compounder.
38.3% net margin and 23.1% YoY net income growth on manageable $40.3B debt is attractive, though slightly lower conviction given narrower margin expansion versus S10/S05.
Revenue up 16.6% and net income up 76.7% are encouraging, but 16.7% net margin and $122.6B of total debt leave limited margin of safety if growth slows.
Solid 16.6% revenue growth and 26.6% margin, but $82.7B debt is elevated; I'd need to see leverage declining before upgrading.
22.2% revenue growth and 27.2% net income growth are solid, but 14.6% margin and $36.2B debt on only $17.4B revenue imply high leverage that could compress earnings.

18.5% margin and 7.4% revenue growth are steady but unexciting; $23.9B debt on $21.2B quarterly revenue is manageable but not compelling.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin on near-flat revenue; I need to see margin recovery above 8% before reconsidering.
Only 2.0% revenue growth, 5.6% net margin, and $77.9B of debt signal no near-term earnings catalyst and elevated balance-sheet risk.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% but Sticky 3.5% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue for Defensive Tilt
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—rates unchanged for three months at 3.75% upper bound after 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, yet CPI running at 3.5% YoY (June print 332.57) keeps further easing off the table. The 10y yield has climbed 29 bps over three months to 4.55%, while the 10y-2y spread has compressed 13 bps to +0.41 pp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer. Unemployment at 4.2% is benign (down 10 bps over 3m), so the labor market is not forcing the Fed's hand. This regime—paused policy, above-target inflation, rising long rates—is unfriendly to duration-sensitive growth and favors short-duration earners like banks and energy, while staples offer a defensive hedge. A CPI print falling below 3.0% YoY or unemployment breaking above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward renewed easing.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth names face headwinds from the 29 bp rise in 10y yields and no near-term rate cuts.
Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve (10y-2y at +0.41 pp) and stable fed funds supporting net interest margins.
Energy names are well-positioned in a higher-for-longer rate regime with solid labor demand and sticky inflation.
Staples offer defensive carry as sticky 3.5% inflation and rising long yields create uncertainty for risk assets.
High-duration growth is vulnerable as the 10y yield pushes to 4.55% with no easing catalyst in sight.
Cyclicals face mixed signals—labor market is firm but rising long rates and curve flattening temper upside.

memos.headline: S06 and S02 Post Positive Earnings Reactions; S09 Delisting Risk Clouds Sentiment
memos.body: I am reading the 8-K flow across the universe as of 2026-07-17 and focusing on narrative shifts rather than routine filings. S06 reported results on 7/14 with a +2.5% price reaction, and S02 followed on 7/16 with a +1.2% move—both suggest tone is turning constructive around earnings for these names. S09 stands out negatively: its 7/1 filing bundles a completion of acquisition/disposition with a notice of delisting or failure to satisfy a listing rule, plus sweeping governance changes—this is a clear negative narrative shift that I would not fade. S05 had an unusually dense cluster of material agreements, bylaws amendments, and officer changes in early June, which reads like a corporate restructuring event whose sentiment implications are ambiguous but warrant caution. S03 took on new debt (6/10 direct financial obligation) followed by two 'Other Events' filings, suggesting an evolving capital-structure story that could swing either way.

views.note: Earnings 8-K on 7/14 drove +2.5% price reaction, suggesting positive tone shift that may have further room to run into guidance digestion.
Results filed 7/16 with +1.2% close-to-close move; modest positive tone but lower conviction given smaller reaction and single data point.
Delisting notice and sweeping governance overhaul in the 7/1 8-K represent a clear negative narrative shift that is unlikely to be fully priced.
Dense cluster of material agreements, bylaws changes, and officer turnover in early June signals restructuring; direction of sentiment is unclear.
New debt obligation on 6/10 followed by two Other Events filings; capital-structure narrative is evolving and tone could break either way.
Routine shareholder vote and officer change filings with no price reaction data; no discernible sentiment shift.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing but Still Elevated; Oil Decline Signals Demand or Supply-Side Geopolitical Shift
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 42% over the past month to 283.91, yet remains 8% above its level three months ago, suggesting a structural overhang from earlier policy shocks—likely trade or sanctions-related—that is only partially unwinding. WTI crude at $80.03 is down 17% over three months, which in a geopolitical context could reflect eased supply-chain fears, relaxed sanctions enforcement, or weakening demand from China; I lack granular GDELT event data to distinguish these drivers, so my conviction is moderate. HY spreads at 2.71% are tight and stable, and VIX at 16.73 is benign, indicating credit and equity markets are not pricing imminent geopolitical escalation. S06 has filed five 8-Ks in the past two months—an unusually high cadence that could signal restructuring, regulatory engagement, or supply-chain repositioning, warranting close monitoring. Without explicit sanctions, export-control, or China-policy headlines in the evidence, I treat the current environment as a cautious all-clear, but a reversal in the EPU trend or a spike in oil above $90 would change my view.

views.note: Unusually high 8-K filing cadence (five in ~7 weeks) may reflect material corporate or regulatory developments that could cut either way geopolitically.
Two 8.01 filings in a month are unremarkable on their own; no evidence of direct sanctions or export-control exposure, so I stay neutral pending detail.
Reg FD disclosure alongside Other Events in early June suggests proactive investor communication; benign macro backdrop (tight HY spreads, falling EPU) supports a cautious long.
Recent Reg FD filing on July 14 is noted but without content detail; stable VIX and credit conditions provide no geopolitical red flag, keeping me neutral.
Single 8.01 filing in June with no further activity; the 17% oil price decline over three months could be a tailwind if S10 is energy-consuming, but I lack sector clarity.
One Reg FD disclosure in June; no geopolitical signal distinguishable from routine corporate communication.
